Here is a snapshot of the "About" information for /v/whatever. The first row is titled "Distinct User Counts", which would seem to imply that these numbers apply to unique users. I found this personally surprising at first, because I did not think that almost a thousand unique users posted to /v/whatever in the span of only 1 month.

So I thought I'd investigate.

Using the information so wonderfully documented in /v/VoatStatistics (thanks, @SearchVoat) I was able to organize the following data:

Date Number of Submissions Source
February 25th, 2018 133 Source
February 18th, 2018 132 Source
February 22nd, 2018 185 Source
March 7th, 2018 143 Source
March 9th, 2018 135 Source
March 10th, 2018 111 Source
March 11th, 2018 121 Source
March 12th, 2018 146 Source
March 13th, 2018 142 Source
March 14th, 2018 151 Source

Note that the above information totals all submissions made to a subverse on a specific day; it does not account for unique submitters. As you can see, the sum of the "Number of Submissions" column is 1399, which is greater than the 920 figure given for "User Post Count" in the snapshot I took -- and this is only using data from ten days. Seeing as the 920 figure refers to "User Posts" over the past 30 days, I can only conclude that this figure refers to unique users (assuming I'm interpreting this correctly).

That's quite a number of unique users to be submitting content to a single subverse. I find that impressive and surprising.

I remember that forums such as these often are considered to follow a certain rule: 99 - 9 - 1, meaning that 99% of all users of the forum lurk (they don't contribute any content or comments); 9% of all users contribute comments to the forum; and 1% of the entire userbase contributes direct content.

Let's say this 920 figure is 1000, for the sake of easy calculations. If 1000 is considered to be 1% of Voat's userbase, that would mean the entire userbase comprises 10,000,000 unique users.

This 99 - 9 - 1 is of course not a hard and fast rule; Voat being a forum that encourages new users to contribute in order to have full access to various features and I assume a larger percent of the userbase contributes content and comments. Still, I find these numbers very interesting.

Stay vigilant, goats.
